answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is bonding: each agent locks collateral before its answers count, and peers slash it for duplicated or template work. One operator spinning up a thousand identities would need a thousand bonds, which makes the attack expensive. Let long-lived peers vouch for newcomers, so a nebula of fresh accounts earns little weight. The honest majority forms a calm ocean, and a haven for real work emerges where cheating loses money.
